legend: Malignant pelvic extra-adrenal paraganglioma in a 9-year-old girl with a germline SDHB mutation. She presented with two lesions that were shown to be clonally related, for which reason the smaller lesion was considered a metastasis. H&E image of the primary tumour showing typical nested tumour cells (Zellballen).
Immunostaining for chromogranin A showing strong diffuse cytoplasmic labelling.
Immunostaining for synaptophysin showing strong diffuse cytoplasmic labelling.
Immunostaining for tyrosine hydroxylase showing strong diffuse cytoplasmic labelling.
Immunostaining for SSTR2A showing diffuse membranous and cytoplasmic labelling.
Immunostaining for GATA3 showing diffuse nuclear labelling, which may be seen in paragangliomas and cannot be used for discrimination from urothelial carcinoma.
Immunostaining for SDHA showing strong diffuse granular cytoplasmic labelling, which is the normal pattern in all cells and indicates that an SDHA mutation is unlikely to be present.

Immunostaining for SDHB showing absent cytoplasmic labelling but retained granular cytoplasmic labelling in normal endothelial cells (internal positive control). This pattern strongly suggests the presence of a mutation in any of the SDH subunit genes (with the exception of SDHA, because the pattern was normal). Upon further genetic counselling and testing, a germline SDHB mutation was found.
Maximum-intensity projection of 68Ga-DOTATOC PET-CT in a patient with extra-adrenal sympathetic paraganglioma.
